plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partition + DE
plan.analytical_narrative: Twelve adipose bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated, 6 control), raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples after dropping any non-sample columns), with sex and age recorded per sample and no batch structure. The question has two parts. First, before testing treated vs control, quantify how much of the per-gene expression variance is explained by condition, sex, and age individually — this is a variancePartition mixed-model diagnostic run on voom log-CPM values, with condition and sex as random-effect grouping variables and age as a fixed effect, reported as a distribution of variance-explained shares across genes. This tells us whether age or sex is a competing driver of variance that the DE model must adjust for. Second, run the confirmatory DE test: DESeq2 Wald test on raw counts with design ~ sex + age (centered) + condition, explicit reference level (control), apeglm shrinkage of the condition log2 fold change, BH-adjusted p-values at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering. QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) precedes the model to check for outliers or unexpected structure before either analysis. Enrichment (fgsea preranked on the Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome, from the reference store) follows the DE test to give pathway-level context to the treated vs control differences. A report step consolidates variance-partition results, DE results, and enrichment results with full reproducibility reporting (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions). The counts are delivered as a gene-level table from Salmon with no per-sample quantification files or transcript-length table provided, so the length offset cannot be reconstructed; the DE step fits the count model on the counts as delivered and the report states this limitation explicitly, per the grounded caveat on model_design.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
